summary: The team is juggling urgent operational fixes with strategic launches, with the China Going-Global report and Asia Star/Intelligent China SEO as top priorities.
summaryDetail: The most pressing issue this week is resolving the Outlook account lockout across all devices, which is blocking team communication and requires immediate coordination with JSB for backend unlock. Meanwhile, the China Going-Global report with IE is on track for a September launch, with final content compilation and partner confirmations due by end of July. In parallel, the website redesign is moving forward with a more editorial layout, and SEO efforts are being concentrated on Asia Star and Intelligent China, with audience analysis and conversion tracking setup in progress. The team is also expediting the social media agency selection, with Media Minds as the likely choice, and preparing for the Tech In Asia collaboration. Key deadlines this week include reviewing AI-generated meta-descriptions, testing the new chatbot, and finalizing the report document with Dean Li Haitao's article.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel from the knowledge website homepage.
Integrate videos into topic-based sections rather than a separate category.
Keep the two-menu structure with a knowledge menu and a school menu.
Adopt a more editorial layout to display more articles on the homepage.
Include indices (e.g., BCI, BSI) on the knowledge homepage.
Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top two program priorities.
US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) will be deprioritized initially, with Berkeley as a possible third priority.
Website menu categorization by topics is approved.
Only one press release for Shun Tian Shu will be produced.
Media Minds is likely the best agency choice given budget and timeline.
The report will be jointly published by CKGSB and IE, with the main research from Professor Leeway as the feature.
